Fleet owner overview

See how BOF organizes fleet back-office pressure.

This overview shows how BackOfficeFleet turns trucking back-office operations into visible records, owners, statuses, and next actions. Fleet teams can use the same operating layer to track driver readiness, document gaps, proof packets, settlements, claims follow-up, and administrative exceptions without relying on memory or scattered inboxes.

Trip readiness doctrine

BOF reviews the load at the start, middle, and end of the trip.

Readiness is not just document storage. BOF keeps the release gate, active-trip watch items, closing packet, owner, and consequence visible so dispatch, safety, billing, and settlements are not guessing from disconnected uploads.

Release control standard

No load releases until the driver, carrier, equipment, cargo, route, facility, and commercial packet are ready. No load closes until delivery proof, asset return, claim review, settlement, billing, and archive are complete.

Start

Start readiness review

Before release, BOF checks commercial terms, driver, carrier, equipment, cargo, facility, route, accessorials, and the final release decision.

Middle

Middle readiness review

While the load is active, BOF watches pickup proof, securement, route/HOS risk, equipment exceptions, accessorial capture, and claim signals.

End

End readiness review

Before close, BOF checks POD quality, cargo outcome, asset return, defect status, billing support, settlement readiness, archive, and next-load availability.

Start readiness review

Before the load releases, every gate gets an operating consequence.

Equipment readiness stays separate from driver readiness. Load packet readiness stays separate from equipment readiness. BOF shows which gate is ready, which gate needs review, and which gate holds the load.

DVIR handling

BOF uses last DVIR review and open defect clearance in the start packet. A no-defect confirmation may be recorded by company policy, but BOF does not present a formal DVIR as a universal requirement for every property-carrying load.

Load packet readiness

The release packet carries commercial terms, customer instructions, BOL expectations, accessorial rules, and required proof. That packet is separate from the equipment condition check.

Middle readiness review

While the load is active, BOF keeps watch items attached to the trip.

Middle readiness turns in-transit signals into operating decisions: ready, watch, review, or hold. The goal is to capture proof while the facts are fresh, not rebuild the trip after delivery.

Claim watchSeal mismatch, shortage, damage, rejected freight, temperature issueClaim indicators trigger review before delivery proof, billing, or settlement closes the record.Review

End readiness review

The load does not close just because it delivered.

BOF treats delivery as the start of the closeout review, not the end of the work. The trip closes only after proof, claim, settlement, billing, asset, and archive records support the final answer.

GateEvidenceConsequenceDecision
POD quality reviewSignature, timestamp, receiver name, BOL matchBilling waits if the POD does not prove the delivery event clearly.Review
Cargo outcomeClear, damaged, short, rejected, temperature issueClaim review opens before the load is treated as clean.Watch
Asset returnEmpty trailer photo, trailer condition, drop/yard confirmationEquipment is not available for the next load until return and condition are visible.Review
Post-trip defect reviewDriver defect report, DVIR if required, maintenance notes, equipment photosNext load is blocked if a safety defect remains unresolved.Hold
Accessorial proofLumper, detention, layover, washout, tollsUnproven accessorials stay out of billing and settlement until support is attached.Review
Claim reviewSeal mismatch, cargo damage, facility damage, incident evidenceSettlement and billing stay in review until claim exposure is documented or cleared.Watch
Settlement packetDriver/carrier pay, deductions, reimbursementsDriver or carrier settlement does not release until proof and exceptions are reconciled.Review
Billing and factoring packetInvoice, rate confirmation, signed POD, lumper/detention proof, claim clearanceBilling waits until POD, accessorial, claim, and settlement records clear.Review
ArchiveFinal trip file and audit trailThe load closes only after the record is complete enough for later review.Ready
Next-load readinessDriver and equipment availability after closeoutThe next assignment waits if driver, equipment, defect, or document status is not clear.Watch

Post-trip defect review

BOF captures post-trip DVIR if a defect exists, plus maintenance notes and equipment photos. If no defect is reported, BOF can record that company-policy confirmation without turning it into a universal DVIR claim.

Billing/factoring readiness

The invoice, rate confirmation, signed POD, lumper or detention proof, settlement notes, and claim clearance stay together so billing does not outrun the operating record.

Fleet consequence

TMS-LD-10482 is not blocked by safety or carrier readiness.

The remaining decision is narrow and visible: approve the BOL image, then release the trip packet. Your team can see how a complex back-office process becomes one controlled action.

Ready records
